methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms, a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick, has raised $1.7B to date. The target operates within a sector containing one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method due to data constraints. The Stage-Progression approach applied a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement to the $1.7B capital-raised proxy, implying a valuation of $2.0B. A Peer-Median approach was not applicable; while ten same-sector robotics peers exist, none met the narrow filters required (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability), and a broad sector median would lack relevance. Triangulation across the available method yields a range of $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (high), centered on $2.0B.

The analysis supports a median valuation estimate of $2.0B, with reasonable bounds spanning $1.7B to $2.3B. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of tight stage and valuation-tier peer comparables, limiting cross-validation. The single quantitative anchor—stage-progression mechanics—should be stress-tested against actual recent funding rounds and investor pricing in the robotics subsector as additional data becomes available.
